title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook centralizes guidance, templates, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues we see in customer-facing SDKs and examples. The goal is consistency across the docs site, faster onboarding for engineers and customers, and fewer support escalations.

Scope

- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and copy-paste templates (CLI, serverless, backend integration)
- API examples (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming, function calls)
- Docs site operating procedures (publishing flow, CI checks, review SLAs, rollback)
- Top support issues + canonical fixes and mitigations

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary owner: Developer Experience (devex) team, eng-developer-experience
- Doc owner: Aisha Patel (author)
- Reviewers: Marco Ruiz (SDK lead), Leah Cohen (Docs site), Omar Haddad (Support lead)
- Pager for doc-site incidents: #devex-ops on Slack

Standards and Conventions

- Writing style: single-source, second-person where helpful, short paragraphs, code-first examples.
- File names: short, hyphenated, lower-case, include year when appropriate (e.g., python-sdk-quickstart-2025.md).
- Code blocks: include language tag, use minimal reproducible examples, and avoid long Lorem ipsum snippets.
- API examples: must include request, expected response (truncated), and common failure modes.
- Maintenance: every SDK guide and quickstart must have an owner and an automated link-check job.

Templates and Canonical Snippets

1) SDK Guide Template (use this as README for each SDK)

- Title
- Short description (1-2 sentences)
- Quickstart (copy-paste)
- Auth and config (environment vars, credentials, region)
- Core concepts (client, requests, streaming, pagination)
- Examples (sync/async, error handling)
- Troubleshooting (top 5 support issues for the SDK)
- Changelog and compatibility notes
- Ownership (team, tech contact, support rotation)

Example Python quickstart (copy-paste):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-2.1", prompt="Write a short haiku about latency.")
print(resp.text)
```

Notes: keep examples under 30 lines and guard long-running calls with a timeout.

2) TypeScript/Node quickstart (npm install + minimal app)

- npm install @redwood-ai/sdk
- show fetch/streaming example

Example: (snippet)

```ts
import { Redwood } from "@redwood-ai/sdk"
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const result = await client.chat.create({ model: "gptx-chat-1", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Summarize recent infra changes." }] })
console.log(result.choices[0].message.content)
```

API Examples Requirements

- Each example must include: purpose, minimal setup steps, request example, expected response schema (short), and common errors with quick fixes.
- Include both sync and streaming examples where applicable.
- For function/tool calling examples: include a sample tool schema and expected call-back handling.

Docs Site Operating Procedures (Docs CI and Publishing)

Purpose: maintain high-quality, up-to-date docs with predictable publishing flow and safe rollbacks.

1) Branching and PR workflow

- All doc changes must be authored in feature branches prefixed with doc/: e.g., doc/sdk-python-add-streaming
- PR template must include: summary, testing steps, affected pages, and rollout notes.
- Review SLA: 5 business days (assign reviewer from docs rotation).

2) CI Jobs (devex-docs-ci)

- lint-docs: runs markdownlint and prose-linter (fail on high severity).
- link-check: runs broken-link-checker and reports to PR.
- build-site: runs static site generator (Hugo) and a preview deploy to staging (docs-staging.redwood.ai).
- accessibility-check: basic axe-core checks on critical pages.

Command examples (local preview):

- Install deps: yarn install --cwd docs-site
- Run local server: yarn --cwd docs-site start
- Run link checker: yarn --cwd docs-site link-check

3) Publish and Rollout

- Merged PR triggers build pipeline and deploy to staging. Manual QA step: docs rotation engineer signs off in PR comment.
- After staging sign-off, merge to main triggers production deploy with Canary: 10% of traffic for 15 minutes, monitor errors and site latency.
- Rollback: revert the merge commit; production deploy runs automatically.

4) Emergency rollback playbook

- If site build breaks or critical content is incorrect, open a P0 incident and tag #devex-ops.
- Run: `scripts/deploy-rollback.sh --to-release <last-known-good>`
- Notify: #platform-status and affected docs owners.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (2023-2025 summary)

Issue A: Missing or invalid API key errors in quickstarts
- Symptom: users copy quickstart but get 401 / "invalid API key" within first 2 minutes.
- Root cause: quickstart examples omit explicit env var instructions or use placeholder keys without guidance.
- Canonical fix: update quickstarts to include clear auth block and failing example and add a FAQ note.
- Example auth block: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"<YOUR_KEY>\"`
- Owner: SDK docs authors; verify via link-check job.

Issue B: Streaming examples hang or timeout in Node SDK
- Symptom: long-running streaming example appears to never return and users report stuck Promises.
- Root cause: missing abort signal/timeouts in examples; older Node versions with different stream semantics.
- Canonical fix: add explicit AbortController usage and a recommended Node version (>=16.15). Provide a synchronous fallback snippet and test in CI.
- Owner: SDK team; add test in devex-docs-ci (smoke-streaming).

Issue C: Out-of-date model names or parameters in examples
- Symptom: 400 errors referencing unknown model id or deprecated params.
- Root cause: models change quickly; examples are not pinned to a model catalog release.
- Canonical fix: reference model catalog version in examples and include `model: \"redwood-2.1\"` with a comment pointing to catalog URL. Add a monthly sweep job to flag deprecated models.
- Owner: Model Onboarding + DevEx docs.

Issue D: Confusing function/tool-calling examples (schema mismatch)
- Symptom: tools invoked successfully but results misparsed due to mismatched JSON schema in example.
- Root cause: examples use simplified schema in docs but production SDK enforces stricter typing.
- Canonical fix: include full JSON schema example and a validation snippet. Provide a minimal end-to-end example including request, tool schema, and expected tool call response.

Example canonical fix snippet (schema validation):

```js
const toolSchema = {
  name: "weather",
  parameters: { type: "object", properties: { location: { type: "string" } }, required: ["location"] }
}
// Validate before calling tool
validateAgainstSchema(payload, toolSchema)
```

Maintenance and Review Practices

- Quarterly doc audit: each doc must be touched or marked "verified" every 90 days. The audit report is maintained in the devex shared drive and summarized to the Docs rotation.
- Ownership changes: team leads must update the ownership block in docs when on-call rotations change.
- CI: add smoke tests for all SDK quickstarts (minimal run) to detect breaking API changes early.

Metrics and Success Criteria

Track the following KPIs monthly:
- Docs CI pass rate (target >= 98%)
- Number of support tickets referencing docs (target trend downward)
- Time-to-first-merge for doc PRs (median <= 3 days)
- Number of hotfix rollbacks due to doc errors (target = 0)

Appendix: Common CLI and JSON snippets

- Link checker: `yarn --cwd docs-site link-check`
- Local preview: `yarn --cwd docs-site start`
- Publish: merge to main (production deploy)

JSON example (short) for a text generation request:

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-2.1",
  "prompt": "Translate to French: 'Good morning'",
  "max_tokens": 32
}
```
